newsitem.title: USA: H-P warns of tough comparisons in fiscal Q2.
newsitem.headline: H-P warns of tough comparisons in fiscal Q2.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co executives said on Tuesday the company continued to improve asset management and control costs in its first fiscal quarter, but they warned H-P faces difficult comparisons in the second quarter.

Earlier, the company reported a first quarter net profit of $912 million or $0.87 a share, or about 8.9 percent of revenues of $10.3 billion. In the year-ago quarter, H-P earned $790 million or 0.75 a share, which translated into a net profit margin of 8.5 percent.
H-P chief financial officer Robert Wayman said the "first quarter net profit of 8.9 percent is wonderful -- but the competitive environment will not allow such profitibility for very long."
Wayman said H-P's net profit was the highest the company had achieved in more than eight years, but he added it would be difficult to sustain such levels.

Wayman said gross margins, the difference between what a company sells its products for and what it cost to produce them, are not expected to show the same rate of improvement going forward as they did in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
In the first quarter ended in January, H-P's gross margin rose to 35 percent from 32.8 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.
